audits.title: 606 AUDIT: IV Fluid Prescribing in Surgical Patients
audits.standard: NICE CG174: maintenance 25-30ml/kg/day water and 1mmol/kg/day sodium, potassium and chloride
audits.setting: Two surgical inpatient wards, district general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow)

cycle1.result: Maintenance fluids prescribed for 76%; mean 2.3L/day; net sodium +221mmol, potassium -62mmol, chloride +162mmol (295% excess sodium, 216% excess chloride, 82% less potassium than required).

audits.other_findings: A maintenance fluid prescribing protocol and teaching sessions are planned.
audits.citation: Shakir T, Mills E, Koomson A, Iqbal M. 606 AUDIT: IV Fluid Prescribing in Surgical Patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.072.

audits.title: EP.TU.364Intravenous fluid prescribing – common pitfalls and suggestions for improvement
audits.setting: Adult surgical inpatients on maintenance IV fluids, district general hospital, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Wrexham

cycle1.result: About 50% of patients prescribed appropriate IV fluid volumes; FY1 survey mean score 54%.

audits.intervention: Tutorial on fluid management for FY1s and a fluid management algorithm made available in SAU.

cycle2.result: Some improvement in appropriate volumes and choice of maintenance fluids; FY1 survey score 64%.

audits.other_findings: Previous fluid prescriptions were often copied.
audits.citation: Makhort A, Ma J, Ng S. EP.TU.364Intravenous fluid prescribing – common pitfalls and suggestions for improvement. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab311.045.

audits.title: 944 Re Audit: Maintenance Iv Fluids Prescribing
audits.standard: Trust/NICE guidelines: 0.18% saline in glucose 4% as recommended maintenance fluid
audits.setting: Royal Preston Hospital; junior clinicians and patients prescribed maintenance fluid

cycle1.result: 16% prescribed the recommended maintenance fluid; Plasma-Lyte most prescribed (42%).

audits.intervention: Posters and email reminders of trust IV fluid prescribing guidelines.
audits.other_findings: Junior knowledge (n=21) improved: recommended fluid 52% to 80%, ml/kg/day 66% to 70%, monitoring 52% to 100%.
audits.citation: Sehrazi S, Koroma P, Shetty V. 944 Re Audit: Maintenance Iv Fluids Prescribing. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.049.

audits.title: 595 Audit of IV fluids prescription and administration on adult surgical in-patients
audits.standard: NICE IV fluid guidelines, GIFTASUP and local hospital policies
audits.setting: Dumfries and Galloway Royal Infirmary; adult surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: Only 10% had U&Es pre-checked; 63% of prescriptions for maintenance; 0.18% NaCl/4% dextrose used in 35% and Hartmann's in 30%; commonest rate 150 ml/hr (35%); 25% had complications.

audits.other_findings: Most fluids prescribed by FY1s (40%) and ANPs (20%); hyponatraemia 15% and hypokalaemia 5%.
audits.citation: Babiker M, Garnett J, Dawson A, Hassoun O, Jones K, Apollos J, et al.. 595 Audit of IV fluids prescription and administration on adult surgical in-patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.515.

audits.title: 1039 Preventing Avoidable Harm with Safe IV Fluid Therapy – a Closed Loop Audit
audits.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Regular hydration assessment 10%; appropriate resuscitation fluid 32%; maintenance fluid when indicated 52%; correct maintenance composition 0%.

audits.intervention: Findings presented at a local meeting, posters and regular teaching on safe IV fluid prescribing.

cycle2.result: Regular hydration assessment 28%; appropriate resuscitation 66%; maintenance fluid when indicated 84%; correct composition 15%.

audits.citation: Hassan S, Alam S, Shoaib M, Ibrahim M. 1039 Preventing Avoidable Harm with Safe IV Fluid Therapy – a Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.174.

audits.title: 329 An Audit into the Prescription of Maintenance IV Fluids for General Surgery Patients
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on maintenance IV fluids (25-30 ml/kg/day water; approximately 1 mmol/kg/day potassium, sodium and chloride; approximately 50-100 g/day glucose)
audits.setting: Three surgical wards, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust, Hastings

cycle1.result: No patients were given IV fluids according to NICE guidelines.

audits.intervention: Proforma and teaching to foundation doctors on the ward.

cycle2.result: Second cycle in progress; early signs show a positive improvement (no figures reported).

audits.other_findings: Data collected daily from patient records, drug charts and nurses in charge for nil by mouth patients.
audits.citation: Ravendran K. 329 An Audit into the Prescription of Maintenance IV Fluids for General Surgery Patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.221.

audits.title: 760 Intravenous Maintenance Fluid Prescribing in Nil-by-Mouth Patients in General Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE recommendations for maintenance IV fluids in nil-by-mouth patients
audits.setting: General Surgery, University Hospital of North Durham, nil-by-mouth patients

cycle1.result: Significant lack of potassium and glucose prescribing.

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions for FY1/2 doctors and posters on surgical wards.

cycle2.result: 82% met daily water, 94% sodium and 96% chloride requirements; only 24% met glucose and 16% potassium requirements.

audits.other_findings: Increases of 40%, 10% and 11% in water, sodium and chloride adherence; 55% and 54% rises in glucose- and potassium-containing bags.
audits.citation: Ismail R. 760 Intravenous Maintenance Fluid Prescribing in Nil-by-Mouth Patients in General Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.263.

audits.title: SP3.05 Improving Fluid Resuscitation and Maintenance Prescription Practices in Surgical Admissions: Closed loops double audits
audits.standard: British Consensus Guidelines on Intravenous Fluid Therapy for Adult Surgical Patients (GIFTASUP)

cycle1.result: Resuscitation (n=59): 43% received optimal fluid resuscitation, 36% received no fluids, 34% prescribed non-optimal fluid types. Maintenance (n=53): 74% prescribed fluids, 66% met daily sodium requirements, 47% met free fluid requirements.

audits.intervention: Targeted educational interventions for junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Resuscitation (n=53): optimal fluid resuscitation 83%, non-optimal prescriptions 17%, fluid prescription rate 64% to 94%. Maintenance (n=24): prescription rate 91.7%, sodium requirements 91.7%, free fluid targets 75%.

audits.other_findings: Use of appropriate fluid types improved only from 36% to 45.5%.
audits.citation: Almoshantaf M, Barcelona M, Sheth H, Othman Y. SP3.05 Improving Fluid Resuscitation and Maintenance Prescription Practices in Surgical Admissions: Closed loops double audits. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.039.

audits.title: 65 Improvement of FY1 Fluid Review Quality in Urology Using a Novel Electronic Proforma: A 2-Cycle Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on fluid assessment parameters
audits.setting: High-volume tertiary urology centre, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Fluid balance recorded 38%, heart rate 35%, blood pressure 38%; 27% of FY1s confident in fluid reviews.

audits.intervention: Electronic proforma in TrakCare with NICE review parameters as headers, plus urology-specific fluid teaching for FYs.

cycle2.result: Fluid balance 78%, heart rate 96%, blood pressure 96% (all p<0.01); FY1 confidence 90%.

audits.other_findings: Only 27% of FY1s reported sufficient fluid teaching before starting.
audits.citation: Shah C. 65 Improvement of FY1 Fluid Review Quality in Urology Using a Novel Electronic Proforma: A 2-Cycle Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.204.
